name: Signadot

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: Free forever: 50 sandbox creations/month, 100 test invocations/month, 10 concurrent devboxes, 1 Kubernetes cluster, 1 resource plugin. Hard cap: creations beyond quota are rejected until the 1st of next month (00:00 UTC); add-ons only on Business.

plans.name: Business
plans.note: $250/month includes 100 sandbox creations, 200 test invocations, 15 concurrent devboxes, 3 clusters, 5 resource plugins. Add-ons (pricing-page calculator): +50 sandboxes $300 ($6 per create), +100 test invocations $50 ($0.50 each), +5 concurrent devboxes $200 ($40 each). Self-serve spend capped at $2,050/month excluding the $250 SSO add-on; 10% off yearly; 30-day free trial.

caveats: Free 50 sandbox creates/100 tests/10 devboxes; Business $250/mo includes 100 creates/200 tests/15 concurrent devboxes. Add-ons sold in blocks; max Business $2050 excluding $250 SSO. BYO Kubernetes host costs separate. Devboxes count integrated workstations/CDEs, not purchased VMs.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
30-day free trial of the Business plan (Starter is free forever).

fleet.verification: Public playground advertised without card; production runs in customer Kubernetes cluster.
fleet.tiers: Starter 10 concurrent connected devboxes; Business 15 plus blocks of 5; sandbox creates/month 50/100 separately.
fleet.notes: Connected devbox count includes local workstations/CDEs, not provider-provisioned VM count. Sandbox compute uses existing cluster capacity; account default machine pool therefore null. Do not interpret 50 monthly creates as 50 simultaneous machines.

snapshot_auto.quote: when more than `ttl.duration` time has passed since the sandbox was created, the sandbox lifetime is considered to be expired and the sandbox is deleted.
snapshot_auto.note: A Signadot sandbox is a logical set of forked Kubernetes workloads in your own cluster routed by a routing key; lifecycle is apply/delete (+TTL deletion). No pause/sleep/snapshot concept anywhere in the sandbox spec, CLI reference or release notes.

snapshot_on_demand.note: CLI sandbox commands are apply / get-env / get-files / list / get / delete only; no snapshot, checkpoint or fork-from-state API in CLI, REST spec index or release notes. Absence-based, hence medium.

harness_api.quote: **[Signadot MCP server](https://www.signadot.com/docs/integrations/mcp.md)** exposes Signadot control-plane operations as MCP tools an agent can call directly from its chat surface.
harness_api.note: Integration is the reverse direction: the coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf) runs elsewhere (laptop/CDE/background agent) and calls Signadot via MCP/CLI/agent skills. Signadot does not host or drive an agent harness.

ingress_rules.quote: All preview endpoints are authenticated and require a Signadot API Key or cookie-based authentication to access.
ingress_rules.note: You choose which in-cluster targets get preview endpoints; since Operator v1.4.0 previews can be turned off per cluster or served on your own domain (then auth is yours at your ingress).

secret_proxy.quote: Smart tests can access secrets that are automatically injected into Smart Test Runner pods as environment variables.
secret_proxy.note: Sandbox workloads get Kubernetes Secrets as env/files (spec env/local env secret refs). Control Plane Secrets (KMS-encrypted org store, 2026) are resolved to decrypted values and delivered to plan runners as params ('resolves each named secret to its decrypted value and delivers it to the runner'). No placeholder-substituting proxy.
